subject: Cascade dedicated capacity sizing: SKU mix recommendation and fallback plan
messages:

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking this — we're at the stage where we want to move from eval to a Dedicated capacity proposal. Attached is a high-level workload profile (per-team weekly QPS, peak QPS, percent of long-context generations, and embedding batch sizes). Quick summary:
- Chat/assist: 30% of tokens, median length 200 tokens, 99th pct latency target 250ms
- Batch embeddings: 45% of calls, many small batches (8-64 items), very cost sensitive
- Long-context summarization: 15% of calls, sequences up to 64k tokens, memory heavy
- Re-ranking / reranker: 10%, latency-sensitive but short sequences

We are price-conscious but need predictable latency under SLA. Curious how you would think about H100 vs A100 vs L4 for a Dedicated pool: memory headroom vs throughput vs unit cost. Also want fallback policy ideas if reserve capacity hits limits.

Can we get an initial SKU mix sketch and a rough run-rate estimate for a 12-month reserved commit?

Attached: cascade_workload_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Sam

On 2026-10-11 09:12, Samuel Kline wrote:
> Thanks for taking this — we're at the stage where we want to move from eval to a Dedicated capacity proposal.

Sam — thanks for the profile, that's very helpful. High level thoughts up front, followed by a proposed pilot SKU mix + fallback/playbook. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk through numbers.

Key tradeoffs (short):
- H100 (80GB): best for peak throughput on large-batch generation and quantization-unfriendly models; excellent for throughput-heavy transformer decoders when kernels favor H100. Expensive per-hour but can reduce headroom by packing slots.
- A100 (80GB/40GB): solid generalist — better memory headroom for long-context KV caches and 40/80GB variants help fit 64k-token flows; slightly lower raw throughput vs H100 for some kernels but better for memory-heavy usages.
- L4 (48GB equiv behavior): cost-effective for embeddings and short-turn chat flows; much lower unit cost and lower energy. Not great for 64k context windows if mem-bound.

Proposed pilot pool (12-week pilot to validate ratios):
- L4 pool (40% of reserved v-nodes): handles embeddings + low-latency chat; use aggressive batching for embeddings (batch size 32-64) and prefix cache for chat.
- A100 pool (45%): primary for long-context summarization and reranking; allocate 80GB variants for nodes expected to host 64k KV caches.
- H100 pool (15%): burst/throughput pool for high concurrent generation and synthetic load spikes; also for models where H100 kernels show 1.3-1.6x perf advantage.

Fallback & routing playbook (short):
1) Preferential routing: route to cheapest compatible pool (L4 -> A100 -> H100) based on model variant and slot availability.
2) Graceful degradation: embeddings fall back to cached vectors + queued batching if capacity constrained.
3) Auto-burst to on-demand H100 capacity (pay-as-you-go) for sustained overshoot > 5m baseline with customer approval.
4) Canary model variants: offer a quantized A100 variant for long-context flows if memory fits; fallback to H100 for correctness-critical requests.

Next steps I propose:
- Ops sizing: Kimberly to provide slot density assumptions and cache headroom numbers per SKU.
- Pricing sketch & commitment tiers: Dev will provide 12/24 month reserved vs burst pricing and an example quote.
- Schedule a 30m alignment call this week.

I've cc'd Kimberly for the ops constraints — Kim, can you add a short note on expected KV cache overhead for 64k sequences and a rough slot packing estimate?

— Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Vivek / Sam — quick ops note from the runtime/serving side. See attached latency matrix for internal benchmarks; numbers are conservative and include KV cache headroom.

Assumptions used:
- A100-80GB: can host ~10 concurrent 64k-context single-stream generation slots per node with ~15% KV cache headroom (depends on model tokenizer and kv-dtype).
- H100-80GB: can host ~14 concurrent 32k-ish throughput-optimized slots (kernel-dependent); memory headroom for 64k is lower unless we reduce batching.
- L4-class nodes: optimized for throughput/embeddings; expect ~2000 embeddings/sec per node at batch sizes 32-64 (very workload dependent).

Operational recommendations:
- Reserve more A100 than H100 if you need reliable 64k support. H100 is effective as a throughput overflow and for models where we see H100-specific kernel wins.
- Keep a small L4 pool to offload embeddings and short chat. Auto-burst policies should prefer on-demand L4 and A100 before H100 to control cost.
- Implement per-route token caps and circuit-breakers: if route latency > SLA for >2 minutes, shift traffic to quantized variants or fallback cached responses.

Attachment: sku_latency_matrix.pdf (internal benchmarks)

Kimberly
Senior Technical Program Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Procurement / Sam — attaching a draft quote and a short summary of commercial options. Quick answers inline:

1) Committed pricing (draft):
- 12-month Reserved Commit (pilot mix): L4 (40%) = equivalent 12 v-nodes, A100-80GB (45%) = 6 v-nodes, H100-80GB (15%) = 2 v-nodes.
- Monthly effective unit price: L4 $0.30 / v-node-hour (reserved), A100-80GB $9.50 / v-node-hour (reserved), H100-80GB $15.75 / v-node-hour (reserved).
- Effective monthly run-rate (estimated): $95k - $125k depending on utilization and burst usage. Final numbers depend on exact model profiles and sustained concurrency.

2) SLAs: Standard Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime on reserved pools; per-route 99th pct latency SLOs are configurable. We'll include route-specific SLO clauses in the MSA.

3) Onboarding & Private options: VPC deployment available; typical onboarding 4-8 weeks depending on network review & SOC2 evidence. One-time onboarding professional services fee: $25k (can be amortized in multi-year deals).

Next steps:
- If this aligns, we'll generate a formal PDF quote and DocuSign packet for CAS-2026-092.
- We can also propose a 3-month ramp with a 9-month tail for operational validation.
